record.original_question: Can ultrahigh-energy cosmic-ray propagation and air-shower development reveal Lorentz-invariance violation or other new high-energy physics, and what observable signatures, such as vacuum Cherenkov energy losses, modified interaction thresholds, suppressed neutral-pion production, or sharp changes in muon number, would distinguish such effects from conventional hadronic-model shortcomings?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs), i.e. primary particles (protons or atomic nuclei) with energies E ≳ 10^18 eV that propagate through cosmic photon backgrounds (with target photon energies ε ≪ 1 GeV) and subsequently initiate extensive air showers in the Earth's atmosphere upon interacting with atmospheric nuclei (target mass m_N ≈ 1 GeV). Standard predictions for (i) the cosmic-ray spectrum after propagation, (ii) interaction thresholds (e.g. the GZK threshold for pγ → Δ → Nπ), (iii) the average shower depth of maximum X_max, and (iv) the muon number N_μ at ground level are computed assuming exact Lorentz invariance and conventional hadronic interaction models extrapolated from accelerator energies.

Allow now for the possibility of new high-energy physics, in particular Lorentz-invariance violation (LIV) parametrized by modified dispersion relations of the form
   E^2 = p^2 c^2 + m^2 c^4 + ξ_n p^2 c^2 (pc/E_Pl)^n,  n ≥ 0,
for each particle species, where E_Pl is the Planck energy and ξ_n is a species- and order-dependent coefficient. Such modifications can: (a) shift or remove pion-photoproduction and pair-production thresholds in propagation; (b) open vacuum Cherenkov channels (e.g. p → p γ or e → e γ in vacuum) leading to rapid energy losses above a critical energy; (c) alter secondary-particle spectra and decay kinematics in air showers, e.g. by suppressing the fraction f_{π^0} of energy carried by neutral pions, thereby increasing the muon number N_μ; and (d) introduce sharp energy thresholds above which observables change abruptly.

Problem. Determine whether UHECR propagation in cosmic photon backgrounds and the development of UHECR-induced air showers can probe Lorentz-invariance violation (or other new physics beyond the Standard Model accessible only at large Lorentz boosts and/or center-of-mass energies √s ≳ 100 TeV), and identify a set of observable signatures—quantitatively expressed in terms of the UHECR energy spectrum, mass-composition indicators (X_max and its fluctuations σ(X_max)), muon number N_μ(E) and its energy dependence dN_μ/dE, and arrival-direction distributions—that would unambiguously distinguish genuine LIV or new-physics effects from shortcomings of conventional hadronic interaction models. In particular:

(1) Derive the constraints on the LIV coefficients {ξ_n} for protons, pions, photons, and electrons that follow from the observed continuation of the UHECR flux and from the absence of anomalous vacuum-Cherenkov cutoffs.
(2) Show whether a decrease in f_{π^0} induced by new physics can reproduce the observed excess of N_μ over hadronic-model predictions while remaining consistent with measured X_max distributions, assuming neutral pions still decay quasi-instantaneously.
(3) Identify whether a sharp, threshold-like increase of N_μ over a narrow primary-energy window is predicted by any consistent LIV or new-physics scenario, and specify the experimental sensitivity required to detect it.
artifact.category_tag: Lorentz-invariance violation in ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays
artifact.status_search_result: Recent (2023–2025) literature continues to investigate this question without definitive resolution. New bounds on isotropic dim-5 Lorentz violation have been derived from the non-observation of vacuum Cherenkov radiation in UHE air showers and LHAASO Crab observations, while 2024–2025 work explores whether small LIV could explain the muon puzzle by suppressing the electromagnetic component of showers. No conclusive observation of LIV or definitive disentanglement from hadronic-model uncertainties has been reported, so the broader question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Hypothetical Lorentz invariance violation and the muon content of extensive air showers
status_evidence.snippet: A tiny, experimentally allowed LIV may suppress the electron number in EAS while leaving the muon number intact, potentially explaining the muon excess and its energy dependence.
status_evidence.claim: The muon-puzzle/LIV connection is being actively investigated as of late 2024, indicating the question is still open.

status_evidence.title: New bound on Lorentz violation based on the absence of vacuum Cherenkov radiation in ultrahigh energy air showers
status_evidence.snippet: The absence of vacuum Cherenkov radiation in UHECR-induced showers is used to constrain isotropic dim-5 Lorentz violation in protons, quarks, and electrons.
status_evidence.claim: Constraints on LIV from UHECR observations continue to tighten but no positive detection has been reported.

status_evidence.title: Vacuum Cherenkov radiation for nonminimal dimension-5 Lorentz violation
status_evidence.snippet: 2025 paper deriving vacuum Cherenkov predictions for nonminimal dim-5 LIV operators.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical signatures of LIV in UHECR-related processes are still being developed in 2025.

status_evidence.title: Constraints to Lorentz violation and ultrahigh-energy electrons in D-foamy space-times
status_evidence.snippet: 2025 JHEP paper deriving LIV constraints from UHE electrons.
status_evidence.claim: Active 2025 research line indicates the question of LIV signatures in UHECR remains open.
